name: Leaving Earth: The People Who Went to Space
description: The rocket designers who made it possible and the first travellers beyond the sky, from Gagarin and Armstrong to the women and record-holders who followed.

checkpoints.name: The rocket builders
checkpoints.note: Korolev in the Soviet Union and von Braun, first in Germany and then in America, design the rockets that can leave the atmosphere, while the Cold War turns the project into a race.

checkpoints.name: Firsts in orbit
checkpoints.note: Gagarin orbits the Earth, Shepard and Glenn answer for America, Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space and Leonov the first to walk in space.

checkpoints.name: The Moon
checkpoints.note: Armstrong and Aldrin land on the Moon in Apollo 11 while Collins waits in orbit, and Apollo 17's Cernan is the last to walk there. Katherine Johnson and Margaret Hamilton help get them there and back.

checkpoints.name: Shuttles and stations
checkpoints.note: Space Shuttles carry women and international crews. Ride, Savitskaya, Sharman, Sharma, Collins and Jemison fly, Polyakov sets a record on Mir, and the loss of Challenger in 1986 brings tragedy.

checkpoints.name: Living in orbit
checkpoints.note: The International Space Station is staffed without a break, Yang Liwei flies for China and Whitson commands the station. Columbia breaks up in 2003, killing Kalpana Chawla and her crew, and space becomes a workplace as well as a destination.
